title.narrative: Increased capacity of Member States for the realization of a safe and healthy working environment

description.narrative: Promoting, respecting and realizing the fundamental principle and right at work of a safe and healthy working environment requires sound national occupational safety and health frameworks, as outlined in the fundamental OSH Conventions Nos. 155 and 187. To this end, constituents will be supported through assessments of national systems and capacity-building initiatives and resources, including evidence-based guidance materials, as well as advocacy and awareness raising tools. The following are the major global deliverables and activities of the ILO in this policy area. (1) Follow-up to the International Labour Conference resolution for the inclusion of a safe and healthy working environment in the framework of fundamental principles and rights at work and the reviewed global OSH strategy, including by promoting the ratification and implementation of OSH fundamental Conventions and other OSH standards, and the use of ILO guidelines and codes of practice; strengthening collaboration between OSH institutions and networks; informing global, regional and national policy dialogue; increasing policy coherence and enhancing outreach to build a culture of prevention among multilateral partners, including UN agencies, regional agencies, the G7 and the G20 (2) Updated global estimates on work-related injuries and diseases and enhance the knowledge base on climate change, technology, new forms of work and other challenges. (3) Documentation and dissemination of OSH knowledge, data and good practices, and awareness raising, including through the World Day for Safety and Health at Work and other global and regional events and platforms. (4) Update of the ILO’s normative framework on OSH with regard to biological and chemical hazards, development of guidelines on chemical hazards and update of the code of practice on safety and health in the use of machinery.
